claims.work: Technological Approach to Mind Everywhere: An Experimentally-Grounded Framework for Understanding Diverse Bodies and Minds
claims.chapter: Levin M 2022, Technological Approach to Mind Everywhere: An Experimentally-Grounded Framework for Understanding Diverse Bodies and Minds › Technological Approach to Mind Everywhere: A Proposal for a Framework › Philosophical Foundations of an Approach to Diverse Intelligences
claims.label: Gene regulatory network models exhibit associative learning
claims.statement: Analyses of biological gene regulatory network models show that they exhibit associative and several other kinds of learning, as well as pattern completion and generalization, suggesting GRNs could be trained with patterned stimuli rather than rewired.

operationalizations.text: Run published GRN models through prespecified conditioning, pattern-completion, and generalization protocols, comparing post-training responses with unpaired-stimulus and parameter-shuffled controls.

On published GRN models, pair a cue with an outcome-producing stimulus and test whether the cue later changes the response relative to unpaired controls; associative learning, pattern completion, or generalization holds if the paired network meets that criterion and a shuffled network does not.

obstacles: Learning terminology may map imperfectly onto dynamical adaptation.
Some cited models or parameters may require reconstruction from articles.
Code for the 2021 Boolean memory screen was withheld, so the exact published runs cannot be replayed.
Associative learning, pattern completion, and generalization are defined differently across the cited papers.

claims.work: Darwin's agential materials: evolutionary implications of multiscale competency in developmental biology
claims.chapter: Levin M 2023, Darwin's agential materials: evolutionary implications of multiscale competency in developmental biology › Multiple modalities for computation and control across scales
claims.label: Planaria adapt to barium by changing expression of only a handful of genes
claims.statement: Planaria exposed to barium, a non-specific potassium channel blocker that is evolutionarily novel to them, first lose their heads but then regrow barium-insensitive heads, with only a handful of genes up- or down-regulated, showing that cells can navigate transcriptional space to solve a problem for which there was no selection.

operationalizations.text: Analyze survival, head loss and regrowth under barium together with differential expression before and after adaptation, using preregistered thresholds for the number and magnitude of changed genes. Compare with untreated and acute-stress controls to identify changes associated specifically with restored morphology.

Reanalyze the Dugesia japonica barium RNA-seq with a pre-specified handful rule, for example fewer than 20 genes at FDR under 0.05 and a stated fold change, in heads that regenerated in BaCl2 versus controls. A count under that cutoff would support the transcriptional clause; a count of dozens or hundreds would refute a handful.

obstacles: 'Handful' depends on statistical thresholds and sampling time.
Expression changes may miss protein and physiological regulation.
No prior selection for barium is a historical inference.
A handful is undefined until a threshold is fixed, and the original paper used a stringent fold-change cutoff.
Pooled or few samples limit the stability of the gene list, and the anatomical time course is not in the expression matrix.

claims.work: A scalable pipeline for designing reconfigurable organisms
claims.chapter: Kriegman S 2020, A scalable pipeline for designing reconfigurable organisms › Results › Locomotion.
claims.label: Designed organisms moved as simulated when upright, much less when inverted
claims.statement: For at least one deciliated, cardiac-muscle-powered design, the upright organisms' direction of movement matched that of the in silico design under random perturbations, and inverting the design significantly reduced net displacement both in silico and in vivo.

operationalizations.text: Recompute movement direction and net displacement for upright and inverted simulated and living designs, testing directional concordance and the inversion contrasts with the reported statistics.

For the reported deciliated cardiac design, compare net displacement and heading of upright versus inverted organisms in the simulator and, where tracks exist, in the living builds; the claim holds if upright heading matches the design and inversion reduces displacement in both.

obstacles: Raw individual-level trajectories may not all be downloadable.
The claim concerns at least one selected design, limiting generalization.
In vivo p-values are published, but the trial-level movement tracks are not deposited.
The quantitative claim is for at least one design, so a re-run has to recover that design rather than a new evolutionary sample.

roles: reported trajectories, design orientation comparisons, methods, and statistical results

claims.work: Technological Approach to Mind Everywhere: An Experimentally-Grounded Framework for Understanding Diverse Bodies and Minds
claims.chapter: Levin M 2022, Technological Approach to Mind Everywhere: An Experimentally-Grounded Framework for Understanding Diverse Bodies and Minds › Evolutionary Aspects › Somatic Bioelectrics Reveals the Origin of Complex Cognitive Systems
claims.label: Context-sensitive ion channels appear alongside complex metazoan body plans
claims.statement: Ion channel phylogeny is ancient (many channel families likely predate the most recent unicellular ancestor of animals), and the appearance of context-sensitive channels enabling new bioelectric feedback loops tracks the appearance of complex body plans at the emergence of metazoa, indicating an evolutionary continuum from single-cell excitability to cognition via somatic pattern control.

operationalizations.text: Date duplications and domain innovations in context-sensitive ion-channel families on a species tree, then test their association with independently coded body-plan complexity while controlling phylogeny and genome quality.

Build a presence-absence matrix of voltage- and ligand-gated channel families across unicellular eukaryotes and early metazoans and test whether context-sensitive families originate at the metazoan node, alongside gains in body-plan complexity.

obstacles: Body-plan complexity and context sensitivity require subjective coding.
Gene loss and poor early-branching genomes bias ancestral reconstruction.
Correlation does not establish the proposed continuum to cognition.
Domain presence is an imperfect stand-in for context-sensitive gating.
Channel gains at the origin of animals coincide with many other novelties, so a correlation does not isolate body-plan complexity.
The further continuum from excitability through somatic patterning to cognition is not in these matrices.

claims.work: Learning in Transcriptional Network Models: Computational Discovery of Pathway-Level Memory and Effective Interventions
claims.chapter: Biswas S 2022, Learning in Transcriptional Network Models: Computational Discovery of Pathway-Level Memory and Effective Interventions › 3. Discussion
claims.label: Pathway memory is more robust to edge perturbation, perhaps from selection
claims.statement: The memory capacity of biological ODE pathway models degrades significantly less than that of random networks when edges are randomly deleted and added, perhaps because of evolutionary pressure to handle changing environments.

operationalizations.text: Repeat matched edge-addition and deletion trajectories and compare memory degradation between biological and random models. This resolves robustness, while attributing it to evolutionary pressure requires alternative nulls or comparative selection evidence.

Randomly delete and add edges in biological and random models, rescore memory, and compare the drop. A significantly smaller drop for the biological models would confirm the robustness contrast; a similar or larger drop would refute it. The same curves do not test evolutionary pressure.

obstacles: Edge edits may not preserve valid biochemical kinetics.
Evolutionary attribution is confounded by construction differences.
Edge add and delete on an ODE needs a rule for new kinetic parameters, which can dominate the memory change.
Greater robustness is compatible with curation bias as well as with selection.

claims.work: Collective intelligence: A unifying concept for integrating biology across scales and substrates
claims.chapter: McMillen P 2024, Collective intelligence: A unifying concept for integrating biology across scales and substrates › Introduction › Segmentation intelligence is collective
claims.label: The segmentation clock needs a cell collective to oscillate and entrains grafted cells
claims.statement: The vertebrate segmentation clock depends on collectivity: presomitic mesoderm cells do not oscillate when cultured individually but resume oscillating when cultured together, wild-type cells grafted into non-cycling mutant fish express her1 without cycling, and cells grafted into tissue at a different clock phase synchronize to their neighbours' phase.

operationalizations.text: Compare single-cell and collective presomitic-mesoderm oscillation traces, her1 dynamics in mutant hosts, and phase shifts after heterochronic grafting. The claim is supported if oscillation requires cell density and grafted cells converge on neighbour phase, and refuted by autonomous oscillation or persistent donor phase.

Compare Her/Hes reporter period and amplitude in presomitic mesoderm cultured as isolated cells versus as groups, and measure whether grafted cells adopt the host phase or keep their own. Loss of oscillation only in isolation, and phase-locking after grafting, would support the collective claim; persistent single-cell oscillation or failure to entrain would refute it.

obstacles: The three component experiments span species and laboratories.
Single-cell movies and graft-level traces may exist only in supplements.
The dissociation, mutant-graft, and phase-entrainment results come from different labs and species and are not one downloadable time-series table.
Culture density, substrate mechanics, and Notch coupling can mimic a requirement for collectivity.
Chick and zebrafish are thinner in the published imaging record than mouse explants.

candidate_datasets.name: Gene Expression Omnibus
roles: public time-series expression data can be searched for segmentation-clock cultures and perturbations

claims.work: Darwin's agential materials: evolutionary implications of multiscale competency in developmental biology
claims.chapter: Levin M 2023, Darwin's agential materials: evolutionary implications of multiscale competency in developmental biology › Bioelectric networks as reprogrammable interface to morphogenetic capabilities
claims.label: Voltage is the instructive variable: an unrelated yeast pump can replace tail V-ATPase
claims.statement: Membrane voltage is a coarse-grained, high-order parameter over ion channel and pump microstates: electrogenic proteins can be swapped as long as the bioelectric state is correct, e.g. the V-ATPase function in tadpole tail regeneration can be phenocopied by a yeast proton pump with no sequence or structural homology.

operationalizations.text: Compare tail-regeneration frequency and membrane voltage after V-ATPase disruption followed by expression of the unrelated yeast proton pump, using inactive-pump and voltage-mismatched controls. Rescue that tracks restored voltage rather than sequence identity supports voltage as the instructive variable.

Align yeast plasma-membrane proton-pump sequences and structures with Xenopus V-ATPase subunits, and compare tadpole tail regeneration when the yeast pump is expressed in place of V-ATPase function. Absence of significant sequence and structural homology, together with rescue of regeneration and of the regenerative voltage, would support interchangeability of the voltage state; homology, or rescue without restoration of voltage, would count against voltage as the instructive variable.

obstacles: Matched voltage, construct expression, and regeneration records may not be public.
Proton pumps alter pH as well as voltage.
One substitution does not establish the general coarse-graining claim.
The tail-regeneration rescue counts are in the original experimental paper, not in UniProt or the PDB.
A yeast pump could restore regeneration by changing pH independently of the voltage pattern the claim treats as the signal.

claims.chapter: Levin M 2025, The Multiscale Wisdom of the Body: Collective Intelligence as a Tractable Interface for Next-Generation Biomedicine › Applications and a Roadmap Toward a Radical Regenerative Medicine › Top‐Down Control Exploits Agential Materials by Pushing Complexity from the Engineer onto the System Itself
claims.label: Embryos in large groups form a 'hyperembryo' that resists teratogens better
claims.statement: Individual embryos raised in large groups form a kind of 'hyperembryo' with its own distinct transcriptome and an ability to resist teratogenic challenges far better than individual embryos or small groups.

operationalizations.text: Compare malformation and survival under identical teratogen doses across isolated embryos, small groups and large groups, and test for a group-specific transcriptomic state. A size-dependent protection effect plus reproducible differential expression supports the claim.

Reanalyze RNA-seq from large versus small Xenopus cohorts, with and without teratogen, and test for a cohort-size-specific expression signature. Separately, morphological protection would be scored as the rate of teratogen-induced defects in large versus small groups. A distinct large-group transcriptome and a lower defect rate would support the claim; no expression difference and no survival advantage would refute it.

obstacles: Group density changes chemistry and dose exposure as well as communication.
Hyperembryo is an interpretation, not a separate measured entity.
Raw group-level phenotype data may not be deposited.
The deposit is one species and one teratogen, thioridazine.
Defect and survival rates are not in the expression matrix.
A modest gene list may be a group-size effect without establishing a hyperembryo that resists teratogens far better.

claims.work: Bioelectric networks: the cognitive glue enabling evolutionary scaling from physiology to mind
claims.chapter: Levin M 2023, Bioelectric networks: the cognitive glue enabling evolutionary scaling from physiology to mind › Beyond standard model organisms: stories of plasticity and change
claims.label: Xenopus tadpoles with only a tail eye can see through it
claims.statement: Xenopus laevis tadpoles produced with no primary eyes and a single eye on the tail can see out of the ectopic eye, which can connect to the spinal cord, showing that a frog's cellular hardware can adapt within one generation to a radical reconfiguration of its visual system.

operationalizations.text: Reanalyze blinded visual-conditioning trials for eyeless tadpoles bearing one tail eye against eyeless and normal-eye controls, and relate performance to graft innervation. Successful learning specific to visual cues confirms function through the ectopic eye.

In Xenopus tadpoles with no primary eyes and one tail eye, score visually guided learning and trace axons from that eye. Learning that requires the tail eye, with axons entering the spinal cord, would support seeing through the ectopic eye; chance performance, or learning that remains after the tail eye is removed, would refute it.

obstacles: Raw trial data and connectivity images may not be jointly available.
Nonvisual light responses require exclusion.
One-generation adaptation is inferred from the preparation rather than directly measured.
Published performance is a summary, not trial-level choices.
Extraocular photoreception is the main rival and has to be read off the paper's controls.

claims.work: Transmembrane voltage potential of somatic cells controls oncogene-mediated tumorigenesis at long-range
claims.chapter: Chernet BT 2014, Transmembrane voltage potential of somatic cells controls oncogene-mediated tumorigenesis at long-range › RESULTS › Long-range hyperpolarization suppresses the formation of ITLS
claims.label: Remote Kv1.5 hyperpolarization suppresses tumor-like structures from two oncogenes
claims.statement: In Xenopus laevis embryos, misexpressing the hyperpolarizing potassium channel Kv1.5 in a blastomere distant from the oncogene-injected blastomere reduces the incidence of induced tumor-like structures by about 35% for Xrel3 and about 29% for Gli1, indicating the suppression is not specific to one oncogene.

operationalizations.text: Recompute tumor-like-structure incidence and effect sizes for Xrel3 and Gli1 embryos with remote Kv1.5 expression versus oncogene-only controls. Suppression for both oncogenes near the reported magnitudes supports non-specificity to one oncogene.

Compare induced-tumor incidence at stage 34 for Xrel3 and for Gli1 with and without Kv1.5 mRNA in a distant blastomere. Reductions near the reported 35% and 29%, with voltage changed only at the remote site, would support the result; no reduction for either oncogene would refute non-specificity across these two drivers.

obstacles: Complete contingency tables and individual embryo records are not clearly deposited.
Only two oncogene classes are tested in this contrast.
Raw embryo scores underlying the percentages are not public.
A t-test on incidence proportions is a weak summary, and remote voltage was not archived animal by animal.

claims.work: Technological Approach to Mind Everywhere: An Experimentally-Grounded Framework for Understanding Diverse Bodies and Minds
claims.chapter: Levin M 2022, Technological Approach to Mind Everywhere: An Experimentally-Grounded Framework for Understanding Diverse Bodies and Minds › Technological Approach to Mind Everywhere: A Proposal for a Framework › Specific Conceptual Components of the Technological Approach to Mind Everywhere Framework
claims.label: Planaria regenerate barium-insensitive heads after barium-induced head loss
claims.statement: Planaria exposed to barium, a non-specific potassium channel blocker, lose their heads but soon regenerate heads that are completely insensitive to barium, by transcriptionally regulating relatively few genes; the authors interpret this as cells navigating transcriptional space to solve a novel physiological stressor not met in evolution.

operationalizations.text: Compare head integrity, regeneration, subsequent barium survival, and gene-expression change in chronically exposed and control planaria, testing whether regenerated heads acquire resistance with a limited transcriptional response.

Reanalyze GSE98084 for the fraction of transcripts that change in barium-adapted heads versus wild-type heads, and compare that count with the paper's survival and regeneration tallies in BaCl2; the transcriptional clause holds if only a small fraction of the transcriptome moves.

obstacles: Raw survival and morphology records may not be deposited.
The interpretation as navigating transcriptional space is not uniquely implied by resistance.
Two biological replicates limit how firmly 'relatively few genes' can be reestimated.
Head loss and later barium insensitivity are phenotype counts in the paper, not in the expression series.
Differential expression does not show that the cells searched transcriptional space for a solution evolution had not already produced.

roles: public planarian expression datasets that may include barium exposure and regeneration contrasts
series GSE98084, public RNA-seq of barium-adapted versus wild-type Dugesia japonica heads, for recounting differentially expressed transcripts
